31/G.goal: Explain how somatosensory, haptic, olfactory, and gustatory senses can be perceived and simulated to extend XR immersion beyond visual and auditory channels.
31/G.achieves: It provides foundational human-factors knowledge for understanding and implementing XR systems that aim to support a more complete sensory experience.

31/O1.goal: Explain how human somatosensory and haptic perception can be supported by XR haptic devices and tangible interfaces to create touch-like immersion.
31/O1.achieves: It gives the learner a physiological and technical basis for understanding and evaluating touch and body-sense feedback in XR systems.

31/O2.goal: Describe how smell and taste can be simulated in XR and why these chemical-sense interfaces are technically challenging and less developed.
31/O2.achieves: It helps the learner consider the major remaining senses and their practical limits when understanding or designing for fuller XR immersion.
